articles.title: Homem é detido suspeito de agredir esposa e manter filhos, incluindo bebê de 25 dias, em situação de maus-tratos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Guarda Municipal de Americana esteve na casa da família após denúncia e constatou sinais de violência contra a mulher, falta de alimentos e condições insalubres; crianças ficaram sob os cuidados de um tio materno.
articles.summary: Guarda Municipal de Americana esteve na casa da família após denúncia e constatou sinais de violência contra a mulher, falta de alimentos e condições insalubres.
articles.body:
Guarda Municipal de Americana deteve um homem de 46 anos suspeito de violência doméstica e maus-tratos contra a mulher e os dois filhos, de 25 dias e 2 anos — Foto: Guarda Municipal de Americana

Um homem de 46 anos foi detido pela Guarda Municipal de Americana (Gama) suspeito de violência doméstica e maus-tratos contra a esposa e os dois filhos do casal, um bebê de 25 dias e uma criança de 2 anos .

O caso veio à tona após uma denúncia encaminhada pelo Centro de Referência de Assistência Social (Cras).

Segundo a Guarda Municipal, equipes foram até a residência da família e encontraram a mulher de 33 anos com hematomas nos braços. Os guardas relataram que o imóvel apresentava condições insalubres, além da falta de alimentos para o consumo da família.

A vítima foi encaminhada para atendimento médico, e depois levada à Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Americana para prestar depoimento e registrar a ocorrência.

O Conselho Tutelar foi acionado e as duas crianças ficaram sob a responsabilidade do tio materno, enquanto a mãe passou a receber acompanhamento assistencial e psicológico.

Os guardas localizaram o suspeito no local de trabalho, uma obra dentro de um condomínio em Nova Odessa (SP). Ele foi detido e encaminhado à DDM.

O g1 procurou a Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SSP) de São Paulo para questionar como o caso foi registrado na DDM, e se o suspeito foi preso pelos crimes. A reportagem será atualizada assim que a pasta se manifestar.

articles.title: Itapeva registra 300 mais de casos de virose em setembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Em setembro, foram registrados mais de 300 casos de gastroenterite, segundo a Santa Casa do município. A gastroenterite pode provocar sintomas como diarreia, vômitos, náuseas, dores abdominais e febre.
articles.summary: A Prefeitura de Itapeva orienta a população sobre os cuidados para prevenir e tratar a gastroenterite, conhecida como virose. Segundo a Santa Casa, setembro teve mais de 300 casos.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Itapeva (SP) orienta a população sobre os cuidados para prevenir e tratar a gastroenterite, conhecida popularmente como virose.

Segundo a Santa Casa do município, mais de 300 casos foram registrados em setembro, um aumento médio de 196% em relação aos meses anteriores.

A gastroenterite é uma inflamação do estômago e do intestino e pode provocar sintomas como diarreia, vômitos, náuseas, dores abdominais e febre.

A diretora do Departamento de Vigilância em Saúde, Juliana Ferreira Carvalho, informou à TV TEM que a prefeitura já recebeu o resultado da análise da água que abastece o município. Novas amostras devem ser coletadas e encaminhadas até quinta-feira (8) ao Instituto Adolfo Lutz, em Sorocaba (SP).

Segundo ela, a equipe também investiga os pacientes para tentar identificar uma possível origem comum entre os casos, principalmente nos bairros que concentram o maior número de registros.

“A gente está fazendo investigação com os pacientes, principalmente nos bairros com maior número de casos. Durante as entrevistas, questionamos se as pessoas estiveram em eventos grandes, por exemplo. Todas as informações que conseguirmos nessas investigações vão nos ajudar a chegar a um resultado”, explicou.

Conforme a Secretaria de Saúde de Itapeva, na maioria dos casos, a recuperação pode ocorrer em casa, com alguns cuidados. A principal recomendação é manter a hidratação, consumindo água, soro de reidratação e outros líquidos ao longo do dia para repor a quantidade perdida pelo organismo.

A alimentação também deve ser mantida, dando preferência a alimentos leves e de fácil digestão, como sopas, frutas e torradas. O repouso é indicado enquanto persistirem os sintomas.

Outro cuidado importante é a higiene das mãos, principalmente após ir ao banheiro e antes de preparar ou consumir alimentos. A medida ajuda a reduzir o risco de transmissão da doença para outras pessoas da casa.

A Secretaria de Saúde também orienta que medicamentos sejam utilizados somente com indicação médica.

Santa Casa de Itapeva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Apesar de muitos casos evoluírem bem com cuidados em casa, alguns sintomas exigem avaliação médica.

A orientação é procurar a Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) 24 horas em casos de vômitos persistentes, diarreia intensa ou com presença de sangue, febre alta, dores abdominais fortes ou sinais de desidratação.

Entre os sinais de alerta estão boca seca, pouca produção de urina e fraqueza intensa.

Em casos de sintomas leves ou dúvidas sobre a doença, a recomendação da Secretaria de Saúde é procurar a unidade de saúde mais próxima para avaliação de um profissional.

articles.title: Senac Ceará realiza feira com mais de 200 vagas de trabalho | G1
articles.standfirst: A ação será realizada simultaneamente em unidades da capital, Juazeiro do Norte, Sobral, Quixadá, Maranguape, Aquiraz e Iguatu.
articles.summary: A ação será realizada simultaneamente em unidades da capital, Juazeiro do Norte, Sobral, Quixadá, Maranguape, Aquiraz e Iguatu.
articles.body:
O Senac Ceará realiza, nos dias 20 e 21 de outubro, a Feira da Empregabilidade , que reunirá profissionais em busca de oportunidades e empresas com processos seletivos e vagas abertas. A ação será realizada simultaneamente em unidades de Fortaleza, Juazeiro do Norte, Sobral, Quixadá, Maranguape, Aquiraz e Iguatu .

O evento acontece nas unidades do Senac de cada município e é aberto a pessoas de diferentes faixas etárias, desde jovens interessados no primeiro emprego e na aprendizagem profissional até profissionais acima dos 50 anos.

Ao todo, serão mais de 200 vagas disponíveis, ofertadas por mais de 30 empresas participantes, em áreas como comércio, saúde, gestão, turismo, conservação e zeladoria e segurança.

Horários da Feira da Empregabilidade do Senac Ceará por município:

Sobral (apenas no dia 20 de outubro): 8h às 12h.

O objetivo da ação é ampliar o acesso às oportunidades e aproximar diretamente profissionais e empregadores, além de fortalecer a conexão entre educação profissional e mercado de trabalho.

A iniciativa também busca contemplar a diversidade dos perfis profissionais e contribuir para que candidatos possam conhecer oportunidades compatíveis com suas experiências, competências e objetivos de carreira.

Para o presidente do Sistema Fecomércio Ceará, Luiz Fernando Bittencourt, a iniciativa reforça o papel da educação profissional na aproximação entre trabalhadores e setor produtivo.

“A empregabilidade passa pela capacidade de reconhecer competências, desenvolver novas habilidades e estar conectado às oportunidades. Ao aproximar profissionais de empresas que possuem vagas abertas, o Senac contribui para tornar esse encontro mais efetivo e ampliar as possibilidades de inserção e crescimento no mercado de trabalho”, disse.

articles.title: Traslado dos Carros Círio 2026: veja o percurso e horários | G1
articles.standfirst: Concentração começa às 18h, na Praça Santuário, e saída está prevista para as 20h. Cortejo terá a Imagem Peregrina e 14 carros, com destino ao Complexo Porto Futuro.
articles.summary: O Traslado dos Carros do Círio 2026 sai da Praça Santuário às 20h rumo ao Porto Futuro, reunindo a Imagem Peregrina e 14 ícones em um percurso de 5,5 km.
articles.body:
O Traslado dos Carros, primeira romaria oficial do Círio 2026, será realizado nesta quarta-feira (7). A concentração começa às 18h, na Praça Santuário, e a saída está prevista para as 20h, em frente à Basílica Santuário.

A expectativa é reunir cerca de 30 mil devotos no percurso de aproximadamente 5,5 quilômetros, até o estacionamento do Complexo Porto Futuro. O cortejo deve durar duas horas.

Em sua quinta edição, o Traslado terá a presença da Imagem Peregrina no carro berlinda, que será ornamentado por Djan Slaviero, decorador principal do Círio 2026. Os 14 carros seguirão atrás da berlinda.

Antes da procissão, os carros ficarão expostos em frente à Basílica, a partir das 7h.

O cortejo sairá da Basílica Santuário e seguirá por:

Avenida Visconde de Souza Franco, a Doca;

A chegada será no estacionamento do Complexo Porto Futuro.

A procissão foi instituída como romaria oficial em dezembro de 2019, por decisão conjunta da Diretoria da Festa de Nazaré (DFN) e da Arquidiocese de Belém .

Imagem foi iluminada durante a passagem da berlinda do Traslado dos Carros. — Foto: Joyce Menezes / Ag. Belém

A sugestão partiu do então arcebispo metropolitano, Dom Alberto Taveira Corrêa, em reconhecimento à participação dos fiéis e à importância dos carros como símbolos da festividade.

“Cada carro e cada barca carrega séculos de história e milhares de promessas, e ver as famílias acompanhando esse cortejo à noite, rezando e cantando, mostra que o Círio já começou no coração dos devotos”, diz Mário José Tuma Júnior, diretor de Procissões.

Os 14 carros seguirão atrás da berlinda com a Imagem Peregrina, nesta sequência:

Carro da Sagrada Família: Criado em 2017 por iniciativa do então pároco de Nazaré, padre Giovanni Incampo, simboliza o encontro das famílias em torno da fé.

Carro da Saúde: Criado em 2021, homenageia Santo Antônio Maria Zaccaria, fundador dos Barnabitas, que também foi médico. Em uma das mãos, o santo segura uma cruz; na outra, a imagem branca de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré da Saúde, distribuída a hospitais em 2020. O carro representa a fé unida à missão de salvar vidas.

Carro Dom Fuas: Introduzido no Círio em 1805, por ordem da rainha D. Maria I, recorda o milagre de Dom Fuas Roupinho, nobre português salvo de um precipício pela Virgem em 1182. Também remete ao milagre do Brigue São João Batista.

Carros dos Anjos: Surgiram em 1972 para conduzir com segurança crianças vestidas de anjos, atendendo aos promesseiros. Atualmente, os quatro carros reúnem cerca de 200 crianças no dia do Círio.

Barca Portuguesa: É uma xávega tradicional de Aveiro, em Portugal, enviada em 1971. Representa o instrumento de “pescar cristãos”.

Barca com Velas: Criada em 1982 e doada por Chico Fonseca, representa o chamado à fé cristã, assim como os demais barcos do Círio.

Barca Nova, Barca com Remos e Cesto de Promessas: Mantêm o simbolismo de “pescar cristãos”. O Cesto de Promessas recebe pedidos e agradecimentos dos fiéis, que, após a festividade, são queimados em uma cerimônia especial.

articles.title: Peça sobre envelhecimento é apresentada por artista de 80 anos no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Pela primeira vez no Acre, artista de 80 anos convida público para reflexão com leveza. O espetáculo ocorre nesta quinta-feira (8), às 19h30, no Sesc Centro, na capital acreana.
articles.summary: Pela primeira vez no Acre, artista de 80 anos convida público para reflexão com leveza. O espetáculo ocorre nesta quinta-feira (8), às 19h30, no Sesc Centro, na capital acreana.
articles.body:
"Venham e vamos brindar e dar viva a vida. É um prazer imenso estar aqui no Acre, eu, uma velha de 80 anos, estreei o espetáculos aos 70 e tenho um prazer imenso de olhar olho no olho cada um que for me assistir, é uma emoção falar desse processo encantador e que nos dá medo"

👵 É assim que a atriz e dramaturga Ruth Guimarães, de 80 anos, explica sobre o espetáculo gratuito 'Velhice Ponto G', que será apresentado nesta quinta-feira (8), em Rio Branco . A peça transforma experiências da autora e mostra que nvelhecer não significa deixar de desejar e sonhar.

Ao g1 , a autora e diretora, que está pela primeira vez no Acre, diz que busca combinar humor e poesia para falar sobre envelhecimento, sexualidade, solidão, sonhos e a vontade de continuar vivendo sobretudo em meio ao etarismo, discriminação devido à idade.

A apresentação está marcada para esta quinta com previsão de iniciar as 19h30, no Sesc Centro, localizado na Avenida Brasil, no Centro da capital acreana. Em cena, Ruth revisita memórias relacionadas à passagem do tempo para questionar a forma como a velhice é vista pela sociedade.

Peça inédita sobre envelhecimento é apresentada por dramaturga de 80 anos no Acre — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/ Lucas Sancho

A peça que está em cartaz há 10 anos, parte de situações pessoais da artista para abordar temas que ainda são tratados como tabu relacionados às pessoas idosas. O título do espetáculo estabelece uma relação com o chamado ponto G, uma área apontada como erógena no corpo feminino.

"Poder compartilhar com o público esses meus questionamentos sobre o envelhecimento, etarismo e um país que está envelhecendo é uma mega experiência", ressalta.

Contudo, na peça 'Velhice Ponto G', a expressão representa uma espécie de zona de prazer e liberdade que, segundo Ruth, permanece possível em qualquer fase da vida. A dramaturga também fala de desejo sexual, abandono, solidão, medo da morte, invisibilidade social e sonhos que foram perdidos.

Endereço: Avenida Brasil, 713, Centro, Rio Branco – Acre

articles.title: Santa Casa de São Roque afasta equipe para apurar morte de bebê | G1
articles.standfirst: Conforme a Santa Casa de São Roque (SP), medida é preventiva e visa garantir isenção, transparência e legitimidade da apuração. Caso envolve o filho do influenciador Victor Haak, que denunciou o caso em vídeo e a família registrou boletim de ocorrência.
articles.summary: A Santa Casa de São Roque afastou profissionais após a morte do filho do influenciador Victor Haak. O caso é investigado também pela polícia e por uma CPI na Câmara.
articles.body:
Santa Casa de São Roque (SP) — Foto: Google Street View

A Santa Casa de São Roque (SP) afastou os profissionais que participaram do atendimento ao bebê que morreu logo após o parto na semana passada . A informação foi confirmada pela própria instituição nesta quarta-feira (7).

O caso envolve o influenciador Victor Haak, que denunciou suposta negligência médica após a morte do filho dele em 29 de setembro.

Conforme o hospital, o afastamento ocorreu em decorrência do processo de análise técnico-assistencial em andamento. Os nomes e os cargos dos profissionais afastados não foram informados.

"A medida preventiva visa garantir a total isenção, transparência e legitimidade da apuração interna, reiterando o compromisso da instituição em prestar todos os esclarecimentos necessários à família e às autoridades competentes", afirma a Santa Casa, em nota.

Victor Haak postou um vídeo ainda na quarta-feira (30) para falar sobre a situação. "Meu filho morreu ontem por pura negligência. A gente quer resposta da Santa Casa de São Roque. Por que que meu filho morreu, cara, se ele estava perfeito. Por que demoraram tanto para fazer essa cesária? É absurdo o que aconteceu."

Criança morre durante parto na Santa Casa de São Roque (SP) e família alega negligência médica — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Ele diz ainda que a prioridade a partir daquele momento era cuidar da esposa, que teria perdido muito sangue. "A gente quer explicação, quer justiça. Isso não pode acontecer. Outras famílias não podem passar por isso. O que posso deixar claro é que houve negligência."

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência do caso, feito pelo avô da criança, a gestante deu entrada no hospital na madrugada de segunda-feira (28), sentindo fortes dores abdominais e em possível trabalho de parto.

No final da tarde do dia seguinte, na terça-feira (29), por volta das 17h, a família foi informada de que o bebê havia nascido sem vida.

Com a situação, foram determinadas as providências administrativas para o encaminhamento do natimorto ao Serviço de Verificação de Óbitos (SVO).

A declaração de óbito aponta duas situações: anoxia perinatal (quando o bebê deixa de receber oxigênio ou nutrientes suficientes durante a gestação ou o trabalho de parto) e cesárea por sofrimento fetal (quando falta oxigênio ou fluxo sanguíneo adequado para o recém-nascido durante o parto ou logo após o nascimento).

Logo após as denúncias, em nota, a Santa Casa de São Roque disse que a paciente deu entrada na unidade na segunda-feira (28) e que, após avaliação, foi internada com bolsa rota [rompimento precoce da membrana amniótica], fora de trabalho de parto, para acompanhamento.

"No dia seguinte, diante da avaliação clínica, foi indicada e realizada uma cesariana de urgência. Ao nascer, o recém-nascido recebeu atendimento do neonatologista em sala de parto. Foi constatado o óbito perinatal."

A instituição disse ainda que o caso está sob análise técnico-assistencial interna, com revisão do prontuário e das etapas do atendimento. "A instituição lamenta profundamente a perda e segue prestando apoio à família e à disposição das autoridades competentes para prestar os esclarecimentos necessários."

A Câmara de São Roque abriu na mesma semana uma Comissão Parlamentar de Inquérito (CPI) para investigar o caso. Todos os parlamentares da Casa assinaram o documento que pede a instauração do procedimento.

Para os trabalhos de apuração, estão previstos:

A requisição de prontuários médicos e hospitalares integrais;

O mapeamento de escalas e recursos humanos;

A requisição de prontuários de outros eventos correlatos e de protocolos institucionais e normativos;

Oitiva de testemunhas e agentes envolvidos no caso.

Os vereadores Guilherme Nunes (PSD), Flávio Rodrigues (Republicanos) e Diego Costa (PSB) foram nomeados para compor a CPI. A função de cada membro ainda não está definida. A primeira reunião do grupo será na quinta-feira (8), às 15h30.

articles.title: Trump is fighting Obamacare fraud. Democrats are defending the numbers
articles.summary: Trump's CMS crackdown canceled 315,000 unauthorized Obamacare enrollments covering 760,000 people, targeting $2.2 billion in fraudulent subsidies.
articles.body: Democrats love double talk. They claim to defend affordable health care while taxpayers finance fraudulent enrollments that harm the very consumers Obamacare was supposed to protect. Right on cue, they turned the Trump administration’s fraud crackdown into cruelty. Chuck Schumer claims the administration is kicking hundreds of thousands of people off their plans, while former Speaker Nancy Pelosi calls fraud enforcement a "false pretext" for stripping away coverage. Before Democrats declare 760,000 people victims of Republican cruelty, they should explain why taxpayers were financing policies that some consumers never requested, used and know existed. The Trump administration recently announced that CMS canceled approximately 315,000 unauthorized Obamacare enrollments covering more than 760,000 people and expected to recover approximately $2.2 billion in taxpayer-funded subsidies. An additional 419,000 enrollments are undergoing eligibility verification. Every taxpayer and every family struggling to afford health insurance should be alarmed. Instead, Rep. Richard Neal, the ranking Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, accused Republicans of "[doubling] down to take [coverage] away entirely," warning that the crackdown would increase medical debt and health care costs without acknowledging the fraudulent enrollment or the $2.2 billion in subsidies the administration expects to recover. GAO found that Biden-era controls failed to verify consumer consent, restrict broker access or notify patients when plans changed. Complaints involving confirmed unauthorized activity more than quadrupled from 2023 through 2025. Predatory brokers used basic personal information to enroll consumers or switch their plans without permission, changed their contact information to conceal the activity and then collected compensation from insurers. Victims risked losing doctors or medications, paying higher copayments and deductibles or repaying tax credits based on false information. BOMBSHELL REPORT EXPOSES HEALTHCARE FRAUD SCHEMES AS TAXPAYERS LOSE UP TO $521 BILLION ANNUALLY Democrats are defending enrollment numbers while President Trump is defending patients and taxpayers. Voters care about both fraud and affordability. A recent KFF Health Tracking Poll found that 51% of registered voters consider health care costs extremely important for candidates to discuss, while 43% say the same about fraud in government health programs. Health care fraud is clearly an affordability issue. Every dollar lost to waste or fraud is a dollar unavailable to lower costs or provide care to a legitimate patient. President Trump’s fraud crackdown proves that protecting patients, safeguarding taxpayers and making health care affordable are all part of the same fight. Obamacare was sold as affordable health care, but affordability is measured by whether eligible patients knowingly receive coverage at a price they can afford, not by fraudulent enrollment numbers. Putting the patient first requires the administration to distinguish suspected fraud from legitimate patients caught in an eligibility review because of a missing document, outdated address or administrative error. Anyone wrongly removed should receive clear notice, a reasonable opportunity to verify eligibility and prompt restoration of coverage without losing care. Due process strengthens the crackdown by directing accountability toward fraud brokers who initiated questionable applications, enrolled consumers without consent and then pocketed compensation from unauthorized policies. Under CMS’s recent anti-fraud safeguards, brokers must reverify their identities and include verifiable Social Security numbers or immigration-document numbers. CMS also announced that electronic consumer authorization would be required before a broker make changed to an application. GAO separately recommended stronger consent controls, including one-time passcodes, restrictions on broker access and notifications of broker activity. GAO also found that dishonest brokers could change consumers’ contact information and that CMS only sent notices to the newly submitted contact. To close that loophole, GAO recommended that CMS should alert both the old and new contacts whenever an email address or telephone number is changed so a dishonest broker cannot conceal unauthorized activity. Affordable health care begins with authorized coverage and exposing fraud is not cruelty. While Democrats defend fraudulent enrollment, Republicans should defend the patient.

articles.title: 'I will make you a little star', Katie Price told girl, rape trial hears
articles.summary: Price's ex-husband Kieran Hayler is accused of raping and sexually assaulting a 13-year-old in 2016.
articles.body:
Katie Price messaged a teenage girl allegedly raped by her then-husband, telling her: "I will make you a little star," a court has heard.

Price's ex-husband, Kieran Hayler, is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault against the then 13-year-old girl in 2016 in West Sussex, all of which he denies.

Jurors saw messages sent between Price and the girl, then aged 14, in which Price said she had heard Hayler and the girl had kissed and that he had "tried it on" with her.

"I'm only asking as this is a serious allegation," Price had then asked, to which the teenager replied that it was "just a flirt thing" and that "nothing happened".

In the messages shown in court, Price also asked: "Did he kiss you? I won't bring up anymore just want truth. I will make you a little star."

In addition, she asked the girl if Hayler had ever said he liked or fancied her, to which she replied: "Yes, but I took it as a joke."

Asked in cross-examination as to why she said nothing happened, the complainant, now an adult, replied that she was "trying to brush it off".

Pressed on what she took Price to mean by: "I will make you a little star", she told the court: "I don't think I said anything. I think I just ignored it."

Arlette Piercy, defending, suggested to the court that the alleged rapes and sexual assault never happened, but the complainant told the jury: "I would never make it up."

The complainant said she deleted "I love you" texts exchanged with Hayler after he allegedly told her to get rid of them.

Jurors had heard that after the third alleged rape, he texted her afterwards saying "I love you goodnight", and she replied: "I love you too."

Piercy said it was not accepted on behalf of Hayler that such texts had been sent to her at any time, to which the complainant replied that they were "deleted, long gone, years ago".

Asked if she was the one to delete them, she replied: "Yes, I did. Kieran Hayler was asking to delete my messages."

Hayler was married to Price at the time of the allegations but their relationship broke down in 2018 and they divorced in 2021.

He denies the charges and suggests his ex-wife had "launched a campaign" against him when their marriage ended, and the allegations formed part of that, the court heard.

The alleged victim is not part of Hayler or Price's extended families.

articles.title: BBC's Nicky Campbell tells court teacher who attacked him 'completely lost it'
articles.summary: The presenter is giving evidence to a court examining accusations against two former Edinburgh Academy teachers who are unfit to stand trial.
articles.body:
Broadcaster Nicky Campbell has told a court a maths teacher "completely lost it" and violently attacked him in the courtyard of Edinburgh Academy when he was a pupil there in the 1970s.

The 65-year-old said he was around 15 when he was initially "yanked from behind" by Colin Turner beside a school noticeboard when he was running late for class.

Campbell said he was then "rag dolled" by the teacher and described being shaken, slapped and dragged across the playground.

He was giving evidence during an examination of facts hearing held at Edinburgh Sheriff Court.

Turner and David Bourne, another former teacher, are accused of attacking pupils at the prestigious fee-paying school but have been deemed medically unfit to stand trial.

A sheriff will instead hear evidence in the case and determine whether there are grounds for a conviction.

More stories from Edinburgh, Fife & East

Campbell was a pupil at Edinburgh Academy between 1966 and 1978, from when he was aged five until he was 17.

The BBC Radio 5 Live presenter told the court he was a "skinny teenage pupil" when he was attacked by Turner - who he said was a "physically imposing" man.

Prior to the incident, he said that he and another pupil were looking at a timetable on a noticeboard after the lunchtime break, trying to find out where they should be.

He said there were a few stragglers in the playground but most pupils had gone to class.

Campbell told the court he was "yanked from behind", adding: "I didn't know what was going on, didn't know who it was until I turned around and he [Turner] started hitting me.

"He shook me around and started slapping me. He utterly lost it. It was an absolute frenzy."

Campbell said immediately after the incident it was as if "the red mist lifted" and he and Turner went into a nearby common room and sat down at a table.

The presenter said he told the teacher "I could call the police on you for that" and that the teacher appeared "chastened."

Campbell said he went home with a torn shirt. He told the court his mother saw he was "distraught" and called the school.

Following this, he said there was "correspondence" and that he remembered his mother later saying that Turner had been "dealt with".

Later in his evidence, Campbell told the court that he saw his Edinburgh Academy pupil file for the first time three or four weeks ago.

Asked if there was any record of this incident in it, he replied: "No, it was ridiculously scant."

Campbell will continue giving evidence on Thursday.

articles.title: Mall of America terror plot thwarted, suspected ISIS sympathizer arrested, FBI announces
articles.summary: Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed a mass shooting at the Mall of America before buying an AK-47 rifle.
articles.body: An 18-year-old Minnesota man who allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America was arrested after buying an AK-47-style rifle, magazines and ammunition from an undercover FBI employee, according to newly filed federal court documents. Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud had allegedly spent months discussing his desire to carry out an attack, telling an FBI confidential source in September, "I can’t wait until I kill kuffar man. October 24 is the day insha Allah," according to an affidavit filed in federal court in Minnesota. When the source later asked why he had chosen Oct. 24, Mohamud allegedly pointed to a "Hmong Arts Celebration" at the Mall of America, saying it would have "a lot of people," the affidavit states. WOMAN’S ALLEGED ISIS RADICALIZATION UNFOLDED ONLINE BEFORE CAPITOL BOMB PLOT: COURT DOCS "Mohamud met with someone he believed to be a loyal member of ISIS to attempt to purchase an AK-47 rifle, knowing it would be used in a felony or federal crime of terrorism," Special Agent in Charge, FBI Minneapolis Field Office, Christopher Dotson said at a press conference Wednesday. "Mohamud planned to use the gun he bought in a high-traffic public area just a few weeks' time in support of a designated foreign terrorist organization." Mohamud is now charged with knowingly receiving a firearm and ammunition while knowing or having reasonable cause to believe they would be used to commit a felony and federal crime of terrorism. Mohamud, who was born in the United States and is a U.S. citizen, is the son of Somali nationals who later became naturalized U.S. citizens, multiple federal law enforcement sources told Fox News Digital. His parents arrived in the U.S. through a New York City airport in 2000, according to the sources, though it remains unclear whether they entered on visas or as refugees. His mother became a naturalized citizen in 2010 and his father in 2017. FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital in a statement that the suspect "allegedly obtained a weapon he hoped to use in a mass casualty attack in support of ISIS, but this FBI arrested him and put a stop to his plans." "Once again, this FBI is moving more effectively than we ever have before at stopping terrorists before they can attack Americans – with over 1,100 individuals prevented from conducting attacks, over 4,000 foreign terrorist organization related disruptions and arrests, a 38% increase, and more," Patel said. "We will continue to use every resource we have to detect and prevent acts of terrorism and wipe out their networks all over the country. Thank you to FBI Minneapolis, who did an outstanding job in the investigation and likely saved lives." President Donald Trump also praised the FBI’s handling of the case while speaking to reporters Wednesday. "I did hear about it. And they did a great job. The FBI did a great job," Trump said.Mohamud appeared before a federal judge in Minnesota on Wednesday for an eight-minute initial hearing, according to federal court records. U.S. Magistrate Judge Elizabeth Cowan Wright ordered Mohamud temporarily detained. He is scheduled to return to court Monday, Oct. 19, at 11 a.m. ET for a preliminary and detention hearing. ISIS-K MILITANT SENTENCED TO 20 YEARS FOR SUPPORTING DEADLY 2021 ABBEY GATE BOMBINGMinnesota Gov. Tim Walz thanked law enforcement for acting quickly to stop the alleged plot, saying federal authorities should remain focused on preventing similar threats. "Grateful for the swift and professional action to keep Minnesotans safe," Walz wrote in an X post. "This is exactly the kind of threat we need federal law enforcement working to prevent, and the kind of work that should remain a priority as we navigate a more dangerous world." Mall of America said the news was unsettling for its guests, tenants, employees and the broader community while thanking the FBI and other law enforcement agencies for disrupting the alleged threat. "We are grateful to the FBI and its law enforcement partners for their vigilance and extraordinary investigative work in identifying, disrupting and removing this threat and protecting the community we all share," Mall of America said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital. AMY KLOBUCHAR CALLS FOR MAJOR ANTI-TERRORISM INVESTMENTS AFTER ALLEGED MALL OF AMERICA PLOT The mall added that safety and security remain its highest priority and said it would continue working closely with local, state and federal law enforcement. House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., also praised the FBI’s handling of the case Wednesday after Fox News senior congressional correspondent Aishah Hasnie asked him about the alleged plot during a news conference in Mason, Michigan. "The thwarting of the planned terrorist attack in the Mall in Minnesota today was another example of how important law enforcement is to us," Johnson said. Johnson pointed to cooperation among federal, state and local law enforcement and argued that agencies need adequate funding and public support. "What would happen if that 18-year-old had made it into that mall? It would have been a very different outcome. So we applaud everybody involved in that investigation, all the great law enforcement officers who did their job, and we pray their safety for their safety and that they continue to do that work around the country," Johnson said. The arrest capped an FBI investigation that began around December 2024 and eventually involved a confidential human source who communicated extensively with Mohamud over encrypted messaging and social media platforms, according to investigators. Those conversations initially centered on Mohamud allegedly wanting to leave the United States and join al-Shabaab, the Somalia-based terrorist organization. In May, he allegedly told the source he was "so excited to make hijrah" and wanted to go to Somalia, get married and "fight the enemies of Allah." He said he planned to work for about six weeks to save $2,000 for a plane ticket, according to the affidavit. By July, however, investigators say his plans had changed. Mohamud allegedly told the source he did not have enough money to travel to Somalia and wrote, "so i will do attack here." He later discussed buying two pistols online and going to the Mall of America or the Minnesota State Fair around Christmas, according to the affidavit. DENVER MAN'S ESCAPE EXPOSES CHILLING TREN DE ARAGUA KIDNAPPING PLOT THAT LANDS TRIO IN PRISON Mohamud allegedly discussed attacking the Mall of America with an assault rifle and told the source he could "drive straight to the crowded place and start shooting." In September, investigators say he also sent the source a selfie-style video pledging allegiance to ISIS and its leader. The FBI then arranged an undercover weapons transaction. On Sept. 25, the source told Mohamud a "brother" could sell him an AK-style rifle, magazines and ammunition, and Mohamud allegedly indicated he wanted the weapon to be fully automatic. On Tuesday, Mohamud met the supposed ISIS-connected "brother" — actually an undercover FBI employee — and allegedly paid $600 for an AK-47-style rifle, four magazines and roughly 200 rounds of ammunition. The rifle had been rendered inoperable, though the ammunition was live. During the meeting, Mohamud allegedly said he planned to carry out a shooting at a "kuffar festival" at the Mall of America. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Mohamud left the vehicle with the rifle, magazines and ammunition in a duffel bag and was arrested at gunpoint by FBI agents, according to the affidavit.

articles.title: Christa Pike has pneumonia and no function in her arms after failed execution, lawyer says
articles.summary: The state failed to execute Pike after administering two lethal doses of pentobarbital for a murder she committed at 18.
articles.body: Christa Pike has a “long road to recovery” after Tennessee’s failed execution attempt that left her unconscious and on life support for six days, her lawyer, Randy Spivey, said at a news conference Wednesday. In a miraculous development, Pike awoke and started speaking on Tuesday, but she is far from out of the woods. Spivey described several medical issues, including a blood clot in one arm, pneumonia, the inability to swallow and no function in her arms. “Neither we nor Christa have even begun to process what this means for her mental health,” Spivey said. Pike, 50, became the first person to survive two doses of a lethal injection after Tennessee attempted to execute her last week for the murder of a classmate three decades ago. Doctors have told NBC News that it appeared most of the pentobarbital — the drug used in the lethal injection — entered her arm rather than her bloodstream, having enough power to put her to sleep but not to stop her heart or slow her breathing. As of Monday night, Spivey said it was his understanding that Pike was brain-dead. Life support was supposed to be removed on Tuesday, he said. “But on Tuesday, to the shock of everyone, including me, including her team, and including the medical team, Christa woke up and began talking,” Spivey said. “I do not have an explanation for what happened between Monday night and Tuesday morning.” While Spivey said he was not in the room when Pike woke up, he said the first thing she said was, “Where am I and who are you?” Pike is angry and confused and wants to know what happened to her, Spivey said. He said she asked about her team and about the victim’s family. Still, “she is very aware that the state tried to execute her,” Spivey said. Spivey said that Pike was cooperative during the execution attempt, even helping the execution team find a good vein for her IV. “She was kind and polite as they worked for an hour, stabbing her arm with needle after needle, and then she felt the burn of the pentobarbital, and then she woke up in a hospital surrounded by people she didn’t know with a tube down her throat,” he said. He added, “All of this was foreseeable and foreseen.” “What happened to Christa is exactly what the state was warned would happen,” Spivey continued. Pike’s legal team had fought execution by lethal injection, citing venous issues Pike has that would likely cause issues in a lethal injection. The news conference followed a status hearing in Tennessee court Wednesday, during which Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles ruled that the state must preserve any relevant evidence in connection with the failed execution. “Today’s hearing was just a first step of many to preserve and enforce Christa’s constitutional rights after this unprecedented botched execution,” one of the attorneys, Luke Ihnen, said during a news conference after court Wednesday. “As I said repeatedly, we have not asked the state to turn over any evidence at this point,” he continued. “Only demanding that they preserve it so that her lawyers, experts and the public can learn what really happened Wednesday night.” In court, Ihnen argued, “The state has made no promises that Miss Pike will not be subject to our future execution, and the evidence that we are seeking to preserve now is relevant for any future challenge that she makes.” Myles ultimately ruled in favor of Pike’s team, stating that Tennessee must preserve any and all relevant evidence, including but not limited to: IV lines and needles, medical supplies and records, any drugs used with anything from the manufacturer, photographs, video recordings, handwritten notes, checklists and any witness accounts. “The state will have no problem doing this because you all are already doing that,” Myles said. She said if anything has already been discarded, the state must work to “claw back that information,” and ensure going forward that no further information is discarded or destroyed. Additionally, Ihnen asked Myles to order that the Tennessee Department of Corrections give their team 48 hours’ notice before Pike is moved, to remove her shackles while she is in a hospital bed and to give her access to a phone or a tablet. He also asked that the legal team receive regular visits with Pike, noting they had to wait in the lobby of the hospital for two-and-a-half hours when they tried to see her on Tuesday. Pike was set to be the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. She has been on death row for more than 30 years for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. It remains unclear what her future could look like and whether the state will attempt to execute her again. Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee insisted in the hours after the Sept. 30 execution attempt that the team — whose members’ identities are shrouded in secrecy — followed the state’s protocol well. But days later, he announced that the state’s top prison official, Frank Strada, would be stepping down this month. In a statement, Strada said he believed the state Department of Correction had carried out its responsibilities “in accordance with the established protocol.” But stepping aside, he added, was in the “best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward.” Lee also ordered an independent review of the failed execution and paused all executions in the state for the rest of the year. Pike’s was the second failed lethal injection in the state this year. Tony Carruthers’ execution in May was stopped after the state Department of Corrections struggled to find a vein to set a backup injection line.

articles.title: Iran sends Hezbollah $200 million to aid displaced Lebanese: Report
articles.summary: Hezbollah has received about $200 million from Iran to provide financial assistance to Lebanese families displaced by the war with Israel.
articles.body: Hezbollah has received about $200 million from Iran to provide financial assistance to Lebanese families displaced by the war with Israel. According to a report by news agency Reuters, this marks the first known Iranian funding specifically secured for such aid during the conflict.The funds are expected to be used for an initial payment of $3,000 to around 50,000 families. Priority will be given to people whose villages have been destroyed or remain inaccessible because of Israeli occupation, Reuters reported, citing sources.The money was moved through intermediaries who charged a 20% fee because of the risks involved in dealing with Hezbollah, and the fee was four times the normal rate, the report said. A Hezbollah official confirmed that an amount had been secured and said a plan for distributing it would be announced in the coming days.Iran's foreign ministry, its permanent mission in Geneva, the US Treasury Department and the Lebanese government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.The funding comes as Hezbollah faces growing financial difficulties after Israel's bombardment and invasion of Lebanon uprooted hundreds of thousands of its Shi'ite Muslim constituents. The group entered the regional war in support of Iran on March 2.Despite the scale of the displacement, Hezbollah has so far provided little to no assistance to many of those affected. The group, founded by Iran's Revolutionary Guards in 1982, has suffered heavy Israeli blows in two wars since 2024 and is designated a terrorist organisation by the US.Iran has continued to support Hezbollah financially despite years of US sanctions. The US Treasury Department said Tehran transferred $1 billion to the group in the first 10 months of 2025. Iran has never acknowledged financing Hezbollah.The issue could be particularly sensitive inside Iran as the country faces worsening economic hardship. Tehran's policy of funding regional proxy groups has previously fuelled anger among domestic protesters.Iran had promised Hezbollah more funding after Tehran signed an interim deal with Washington in June that allowed Iran to sell its oil, Reuters reported at the time. The agreement collapsed in July.Washington has since stepped up economic pressure on Tehran by tightening sanctions and imposing a naval blockade aimed at restricting Iranian oil exports.Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem said in a speech last month that the group would soon contribute to a project to house thousands of people displaced by the war, using “available resources and donations”. He did not provide details.Hezbollah's ability to provide local services and post-war assistance has historically helped maintain its support among its constituents. After its 2006 war with Israel, the group quickly distributed cash payments to affected families and helped rebuild parts of Beirut's southern suburbs, its stronghold.This time, however, there has been little sign of reconstruction. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said last month that rebuilding after the two wars since 2024 could cost more than $27 billion.The report did not provide details on how the latest funds reached Lebanon. One said Hezbollah was finding it increasingly difficult to move money through financial companies that had previously handled such transfers.Companies based in Iraq and Dubai were no longer an option, while those in Turkey were also coming under pressure, the report said.Hezbollah's foes believe money is currently the group's “oxygen”, the report added. Despite the difficulty in securing funds, the group has continued paying its fighters and the families of those killed in combat, the report said.The war has exacted a heavy toll on Lebanon's Shi'ite community, from which Hezbollah draws much of its support. Israel has razed villages across areas it has seized in southern Lebanon, saying the move is intended to protect northern Israel from Hezbollah attacks.Israeli attacks in Lebanon have killed more than 4,300 people since March 2, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The ministry's toll does not distinguish between combatants and civilians. Hezbollah has not disclosed the number of fighters killed. Reuters reported on May 4 that several thousand Hezbollah fighters had been killed in the war.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2012, California rebuilt Malibu Lagoon to flush out its oxygen-starved dead zones; monitoring later found cleaner water and a diverse native ecosystem
articles.summary: Discover how the 2012 restoration of Malibu Lagoon transformed it into a thriving ecosystem with cleaner water, enhanced biodiversity, and improved tidal circulation, marking a significant victory for environmental conservation.
articles.body: Malibu Lagoon underwent a major restoration in 2012 after years of poor water circulation, excess sediment and low dissolved oxygen had affected the coastal wetland. The project completely changed channels, improved tidal connections with the Pacific Ocean and removed invasive vegetation. The lagoon was monitored for six months and found to have stronger water circulation, improved water quality, fewer oxygen-depleted areas and a more diverse community of native fish, birds, plants and invertebrates.The lagoon had areas with very low oxygenParts of Malibu Lagoon experienced stagnant water and oxygen-depleted conditions before it was restored. The lagoon had also collected sediment and invasive vegetation, while its altered channels limited the movement of tidal water through some areas. The restoration plan focused on changing the physical layout of the lagoon rather than just removing sediment. Crews modified the channels, improved tidal connections and restored areas with native coastal wetland vegetation. The project also included habitat improvements for fish, birds and other wildlife. The lagoon had been identified as an impaired water body because of water-quality problems, with restoration planners wanting stronger tidal exchange and better circulation through areas where water had previously remained for long periods.New channels changed water movementThe restored lagoon opened additional pathways and went through modifications to improve circulation through the wetland. The intention behind the changes was to reduce stagnant areas and increase the movement of water that was oxygenated.A post-restoration report that covered 2013 and 2014 found that dissolved oxygen at two back-channel monitoring stations remained above 1 milligram per liter during 97% of measurements when the lagoon was closed to the ocean. Earlier monitoring had recorded hypoxic and anoxic conditions in parts of the lagoon. The monitoring program continued even after those first two years, and researchers examined water chemistry, circulation and biological communities to determine whether the physical changes were producing sustained improvements.Native species returned to the restored areasCalifornia State Parks reported that the restored lagoon supported a more diverse community of native organisms, including fish, birds, vegetation and benthic invertebrates, while algae mats that had been widespread before the restoration were also substantially reduced. The lagoon remained habitat for the endangered tidewater goby, and bird use also produced notable results. California State Parks reported that western snowy plovers and California least terns successfully nested at Malibu Lagoon in 2018, and became the first documented nesting by those species there in nearly 70 years. Researchers compared water-quality measurements and biological communities with conditions that were recorded before restoration, which allowed the project team to track changes in oxygen levels, circulation and habitat over several years.Six years of monitoring found broader improvementsCalifornia State Parks said that the restoration had met or exceeded its documented success criteria by 2019, and the agency reported that water circulation and quality had improved, along with changes in the lagoon's plant and animal communities. The restoration was also tested when the 2018 Woolsey Fire sent ash, debris and sediment toward the coast, which added another stress to the lagoon. Researchers continued monitoring afterward and assessed conditions in the restored wetland.The Malibu project therefore produced measurable changes that went beyond the initial construction work. Water moved more effectively through the lagoon, oxygen-depleted areas were reduced and monitoring documented a larger native biological community in the years after the 2012 restoration.You use AI every day. articles.title: Maricarmen dies at 87 after eviction sparked Spain housing protests
articles.summary: Maricarmen became the symbol of Spain’s housing crisis after she was evicted on a stretcher in Madrid.
articles.body:
An 87-year-old woman whose eviction helped stoke nationwide protests over housing has died, Madrid’s tenants’ union said, as trade unions announced a general strike next month over housing issues, which helped prompt a looming snap election.

Maria del Carmen Abascal, known across Spain as Maricarmen, was evicted on September 23 after an international investment fund bought her building and raised her rent by more than 200 percent to roughly $1,880 a month, a move aimed at pushing out the long-term tenant to make way for lucrative tourist apartments.

Maricarmen had been hospitalised after being carried out on a stretcher from the apartment where she had lived for seven decades. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez offered his condolences in a post on X.

“All my love to Maricarmen’s family and loved ones,” he wrote. “A hug as well to all of us who feel this loss as our own today.”

Following Maricarmen’s eviction, the Madrid Tenants’ Union organised protests and encampments in Madrid’s central Puerta del Sol square, drawing tens of thousands of demonstrators before spreading to dozens of other cities.

Trade unions on Wednesday announced a nationwide general ⁠strike over housing issues for November 11, a few weeks before a snap election in which rising rents and evictions have become major campaign ⁠topics.

The country’s two largest unions, the Workers’ General Union (UGT) and Workers’ Commissions (CCOO), said the planned date still needs to be ratified by other unions. It will be the first general strike jointly backed by Spain’s two largest unions ‌in 14 years.

“We cannot ignore the fact that housing is where most of our wages go. What is the point of raising ‌the ‌minimum wage if housing costs are rising three, four or five times faster?” Madrid Tenants’ Union spokesperson Valeria Racu said.

Spain has a deficit of about 750,000 homes, which is set to grow ⁠to more than a million by 2028, according to ⁠the Bank of Spain. The average rental price of 1,176 euros ($1,315) is equivalent to about 98.7 percent of a young person’s average monthly salary ‌in Spain, Youth Council of Spain figures show.

In addition to protests, the failure last week by Spain’s government to pass emergency measures aimed at tackling the crisis prompted Sanchez to call an early election for ⁠November 29.

Sanchez’s main rival, conservative Popular Party (PP) leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo, is seeking a chance at forming a government, while far-right Vox leader Santiago Abascal is positioning his party as a potential kingmaker.

The 54-year-old prime minister, who has been in power since 2018, goes into the election with opinion polls consistently putting him behind Feijoo. The conservative leader suffered a major setback when the party finished first in the 2023 general election without securing enough support from other parties to form a government.

Polls suggest Feijoo will not win an outright majority, meaning he will need support from Vox to govern.

articles.title: Indiana sought part of Jeremy Willis’s property for a State Road 11 project; after neither side challenged a $20,840 appraisal within 45 days, the state Supreme Court ordered that amount made final
articles.summary: Indiana transportation officials sought part of Jeremy Willis’s property for a State Road 11 improvement project in Harrison County.
articles.body: Indiana transportation officials sought part of Jeremy Willis’s property for a State Road 11 improvement project in Harrison County. After neither side filed an exception to the appraisers’ $20,840 valuation within the required 45-day period, the Indiana Supreme Court has ruled that the award became final and ordered the lower court to enter judgment. The ruling was issued October 2, 2026, in State of Indiana ex rel. Indiana Department of Transportation v. Harrison Circuit Court, et al. The court’s opinion, along with coverage from The Indiana Lawyer, confirms the procedural history and outcome. The dispute began after the Indiana Department of Transportation sought to acquire a portion of Willis’s property as part of a project to improve State Road 11. Willis objected to the amount initially offered, prompting the state to file a condemnation, or appropriation, case in January 2025.Special Judge Justin Mills handled the case in Harrison Circuit Court. Willis challenged the taking, but the judge rejected his objection and later denied his request for reconsideration.Mediation became part of the case as the proceedings continued. The trial court indicated that the parties should pursue mediation, while the state maintained that the statutory appropriation process, including an appraisal, needed to happen first.The court eventually appointed appraisers, who submitted their joint report on March 25, 2026. The report assessed Willis’s compensation at $20,840. Under Indiana law, the parties had 45 days after the report was mailed to file written exceptions if they disagreed with the assessment. No exceptions were filed by either side before the deadline, which was May 11. That deadline became the central issue before the state Supreme Court.After the period expired, INDOT deposited the $20,840 compensation for Willis with the trial court, along with $12,400 to cover the appraisers’ fees. The department then asked the court to enter judgment based on the appraisal.The trial court declined. Instead, it ordered the parties to proceed with mediation and later scheduled a hearing concerning possible sanctions against the state’s attorney.Willis’s position was that the earlier mediation order effectively paused the requirement to challenge the appraisal. INDOT disagreed, arguing that the statutory deadline remained in effect and that the appraisal therefore became binding when neither party filed exceptions.The Indiana Supreme Court sided with INDOT. In its unanimous opinion among the participating justices, the court said Indiana law makes an appraisers’ award conclusive when no timely exceptions are filed. The justices determined that the trial court no longer had discretion to postpone judgment or require mediation over damages that had already become fixed under the statute.The court also rejected the argument that the mediation order had extended or suspended the deadline. It pointed to previous Indiana decisions establishing that a trial court cannot relieve a landowner from the statutory requirement to file exceptions within the prescribed period.The justices further concluded that INDOT met the demanding requirements for an extraordinary writ. Although the state had potential avenues for appeal, the court found those remedies inadequate in the circumstances because mediation could potentially result in a different compensation amount or lead to a trial and a new damages determination.In practical terms, the court reasoned, sending the case through mediation and a potential appeal could prevent the state from returning to the $20,840 amount that had already become legally binding.The Supreme Court therefore granted INDOT’s request for a writ of mandamus. It ordered the Harrison Circuit Court to withdraw and stop enforcing its mediation orders, enter judgment reflecting the appropriation and compensation, and release the funds deposited with the clerk.The decision was not unanimous on whether the Supreme Court should have taken the case through an original action. Justices Christopher Goff, Mark Massa and Chief Justice Loretta Rush joined the per curiam decision. Justices Geoffrey Slaughter and Derek Molter dissented, arguing that INDOT had an available appellate remedy under Indiana Appellate Rule 14(B) and chose not to pursue it. The ruling ends the original action in the Supreme Court, with no rehearing or reconsideration permitted under the applicable rules.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In El Salvador’s mass trials, lawyers struggle to defend hundreds
articles.summary: Human Rights Watch says defendants face proceedings where lawyers have struggled to access case files.
articles.body:
Human Rights Watch (HRW) has released a report documenting widespread violations as part of El Salvador’s mass trials, in which hundreds of people can be tried and convicted together.

The report, released on Wednesday, reviews four indictments covering more than 600 defendants and a single court ruling that involved more than 120 people.

It also includes interviews with 15 defence lawyers, who say their clients were denied their due process rights and were therefore unable to adequately defend themselves at trial.

The report concludes that defendants in the mass trials face vaguely defined charges, weak evidence and faulty proceedings. In some cases, defence lawyers have reportedly been restricted from viewing their clients’ case files and communicating privately with the defendants.

“El Salvador’s mass trials are a mockery of justice,” said Juanita Goebertus, the Americas director at HRW, in a statement. “These hearings are designed to produce guilty verdicts, not to weigh evidence under due process.”

The mass trials are part of President Nayib Bukele’s sweeping security crackdown, launched in response to a surge in organised crime in the country.

Bukele first issued a state of emergency to address the crime wave in March 2022, suspending certain civil liberties in favour of greater powers for law enforcement officials. Those efforts included mass arrests.

The following year, El Salvador’s Congress passed a bill clearing the way for mass trials as well, allowing courts to decide cases involving hundreds of individual defendants.

The Salvadoran government has defended the trials as necessary to dismantle gangs, given the scale of crime in the country. But critics have repeatedly warned that such tactics violate basic human rights and have led to unlawful imprisonment.

Bukele himself has acknowledged that innocent people have been swept up in his crackdown. In 2024, he said some 8,000 people who had been arrested were later released.

“We are going to free 100 percent of the innocent people,” he pledged at the time, arguing that no system was perfect.

More than 93,000 people, including more than 3,000 children, have been detained under El Salvador’s emergency order, which has been renewed multiple times since 2022.

An estimated 120,000 people are currently imprisoned in El Salvador, equivalent to about 2 percent of the country’s population. The country has one of the highest incarceration rates in the world.

HRW noted that many convictions in the mass trials are secured by accusing the defendants of being “collaborators” with gangs, a vague legal standard.

In a single trial reviewed by the group, more than 120 people were convicted of unlawful association and sentenced to 30 or 45 years in prison. No one was acquitted, HRW said.

HRW reported that, for the vast majority of prisoners convicted on such charges, the only evidence connecting them to a gang was a statement by one of two anonymous witnesses, who had received immunity from prosecution.

“Prosecutors say a person is a gang member because a police officer says so,” one lawyer anonymously told HRW. “The prosecutor relies on the police report, and the police report relies on unspecified official intelligence or public rumours.”

There have also been questions about the system overseeing the mass trials.

The cases have been presented before the Tribunals Against Organized Crime, a court system overseen by El Salvador’s Supreme Court that critics accuse of a lack of transparency.

The identities of the tribunals’ judges have not been disclosed, even to the lawyers involved in the proceedings.

Still, despite concerns about human rights in the country, Bukele’s government has historically enjoyed a relatively high approval rating in public polls.

Bukele has cited such statistics as a sign of public support for his anti-crime tactics.

In April, Attorney General Rodolfo Delgado also defended a mass trial of nearly 500 alleged MS-13 members, saying in a social media post that the gang had operated systematically for years, causing “fear and mourning among Salvadoran families”.

The Salvadoran government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In its report, HRW called for independent reviews of cases brought under the state of emergency. It also demanded that people detained without credible evidence be released.

articles.title: Leonardo DiCaprio and Monaco's Prince Albert II teamed up to protect the Solomon Islands; their expedition explored one of Earth's richest marine regions
articles.summary: Prince Albert II of Monaco and Leonardo DiCaprio have returned to a shared environmental cause, this time in the Solomon Islands, where they joined a
articles.body: Prince Albert II of Monaco and Leonardo DiCaprio have returned to a shared environmental cause, this time in the Solomon Islands, where they joined a National Geographic expedition focused on marine conservation. The visit brought the Monaco sovereign into the field alongside marine biologist Enric Sala and the team behind Pristine Seas, a programme that has spent years documenting and helping protect important ocean habitats. The Solomon Islands sit within the Coral Triangle, a region known for its exceptional marine life but also facing pressure from human activity and a changing climate. During the expedition, Prince Albert took part in underwater exploration and used the visit to reinforce his support for stronger marine protection.Prince Albert II joins National Geographic team to explore Solomon Islands watersPrince Albert II joined the National Geographic Pristine Seas expedition team during its work in the Solomon Islands in November 2024. The expedition was led by Enric Sala, a marine biologist and explorer who founded the Pristine Seas programme in 2008. The Solomon Islands were a fitting location for the expedition. The archipelago forms part of the Coral Triangle, a marine area recognised for its extraordinary diversity of species and habitats. Its waters include coral reefs and other ecosystems that support both marine life and coastal communities.The expedition was concerned with understanding and protecting these environments at a time when they face increasing pressure. Human activity and climate change are among the factors affecting marine ecosystems across the region. For Prince Albert, the trip also provided an opportunity to see the work at close range rather than discussing ocean protection solely through meetings and international forums.Underwater expedition brings Prince Albert II together with Sala and DiCaprioAccording to Monaco Tribune, during the expedition, Prince Albert discussed marine conservation with Sala and DiCaprio while taking part in an underwater dive in a submersible. Monegasque freediver Pierre Frolla was also involved in the underwater exploration.The encounter brought together several people who have been involved in ocean conservation from different positions. Sala's work has centred on scientific exploration and the identification of marine areas that could benefit from stronger protection. DiCaprio has used his public profile and environmental foundation to campaign on climate and conservation issues, while Prince Albert has made ocean protection a long-running part of his work through the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation.Why the Coral Triangle matters to the Solomon IslandsThe setting matters because the Solomon Islands are located within the Coral Triangle, an area spanning several countries in the western Pacific and regarded as one of the planet's most biologically diverse marine regions.Its reefs, coastal waters and associated habitats provide shelter and feeding grounds for a wide range of marine species. They also have a direct importance for people living across the islands, where the sea is closely connected with food, livelihoods and local economies.Yet the same waters are exposed to problems affecting oceans elsewhere. Fishing pressure, other forms of human activity and climate-related changes can place additional strain on ecosystems that are already sensitive to disturbance. Expeditions such as Pristine Seas combine exploration with scientific assessment, producing information that can be used when governments consider how particular marine areas should be managed.Pristine Seas has been working since 2008National Geographic's Pristine Seas programme began in 2008 with the aim of exploring some of the world's remaining relatively undisturbed marine environments and supporting efforts to protect them. Its expeditions bring scientists and other specialists into remote ocean areas to document habitats and species. The programme has also worked with governments and local partners on proposals for marine protection.The Solomon Islands expedition therefore fitted into a much longer programme of ocean research and conservation. Prince Albert's participation placed a prominent supporter of marine protection alongside the scientists and explorers carrying out the fieldwork.His foundation has also backed efforts to expand Marine Protected Areas and has promoted greater international attention to ocean conservation.DiCaprio and Prince Albert have worked together beforeThe Solomon Islands expedition was not the first environmental project to bring DiCaprio and Prince Albert together. Their public association with ocean conservation goes back several years. In 2015, Prince Albert presented DiCaprio with the Albert I Grand Medal during an official ceremony in Monaco. The award recognised the actor's environmental work.DiCaprio later attended the first Monte-Carlo Gala for the Global Ocean in 2017 as guest of honour. He received an award from the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation for his environmental commitment during the event. The relationship has therefore developed over more than a decade, with ocean protection remaining one of the areas where their environmental interests overlap.The Solomon Islands expedition added a more practical element to that relationship. Rather than meeting at a Monaco ceremony or conservation event, the two were brought together in a remote Pacific setting, alongside scientists and members of the expedition team.Marine protection remains a focus for MonacoPrince Albert has repeatedly used his position to advocate for the protection of the world's oceans. A particular focus has been the expansion and strengthening of Marine Protected Areas, including in international waters where conservation measures can be more complicated to establish.His visit to the Solomon Islands gave that position a direct connection to one of the world's important marine regions. The expedition also highlighted the role of scientific observation in deciding which places may warrant stronger protection.For the Solomon Islands, the significance of such work lies in the information gathered about its marine environments and the wider attention given to conservation. articles.title: Man charged with 13 attempted murders including British child
articles.summary: Abdalmasih Hanoun, accused of carrying out an attack at a French park in 2023, is set to face trial.
articles.body:
A man accused of attacking 13 people, including a British three-year-old and three other children, with a knife at a playground in the French Alps will go on trial charged with attempted murder, prosecutors have said.

Abdalmasih Hanoun is also charged with armed resistance after the attack at a park in Le Paquier, southeast France, in June 2023.

In addition to the four children, who were aged between 22 months and three years, two adults were wounded in the attack .

The three-year-old British child was visiting the area with her parents. She suffered a single stab wound, French prosecutors said, but was later confirmed to be in a stable condition.

Hanoun will face trial at Haute-Savoie Assize Court in Annecy within the next year, the French public prosecutor's office said on Wednesday.

The prosecutor's statement said: "The defendant will have to answer charges of attempted murder in respect of 13 victims, violence with a weapon without total work incapacity in respect of two victims, and armed resistance."

It added that the defendant's mental state had been assessed by a panel of experts, who found he had not been "suffering from a psychological or neuropsychological disorder" at the time of the attack.

This means there could be "no grounds justifying the decision not to indict Mr Abdalmasih Hanoun".

The statement also said that the decision to order a trial to proceed could be subject to appeal.

Shortly after the attack on 8 June 2023, officials confirmed that the four young victims were in stable condition, including the British toddler.

One of the children was a Dutch national and the other two were confirmed to be French nationals from the eastern region of Haute-Savoie.

Two adults were also hurt in the attack, but were later said to be out of danger.

articles.title: Tigray conflict: Eritrean troops move deep into Ethiopia as fighting escalates
articles.summary: Residents of Adigrat tell the BBC they have seen truck loads of soldiers from Eritrea moving south.
articles.body:
Eritrean soldiers have crossed into northern Ethiopia heading towards an area where clashes have been taking place between national army troops and regional forces, residents in the Tigrayan town of Adigrat have told the BBC.

Fighting in the region broke out two weeks ago after months of tension between the government and the party that controls Tigray, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). Both blame one another for violating a 2022 deal that ended a two-year civil war.

Ethiopia has also accused Eritrea of backing the TPLF - something Asmara has previously denied.

The latest unrest follows the launch in September of new alliance of armed groups in Ethiopia, which includes the TPLF.

How fresh fighting in Tigray could spark wider conflict in Ethiopia

The young women who fought in Ethiopia's last civil war and don't want to see another one

Why are Ethiopia's rebels joining forces?

Over the weekend, TPLF forces withdrew from Tigray's main city of Mekelle, which is 115km (71 miles) south of Adigrat and is now under army control.

Eritrea was a key ally of landlocked Ethiopia during the 2020-2022 war, fighting against the TPLF in what was one of the most deadly conflicts this century and which drove the Tigray region to the precipice of famine.

But relations between the two neighbours have since deteriorated largely over the Ethiopian prime minister's ambition to take ownership of one of Eritrea's Red Sea ports.

Last week the two countries severed diplomatic relations as the renewed fighting raised fears of a wider regional conflict.

The BBC is unable to report from Tigray and surrounding areas, though mobile phone connections and internet access have been restored to most areas since the military took over Mekelle.

According to multiple accounts, Eritrean troops have moved from the border town of Zalambessa towards central Tigray, with convoys reportedly passing through Adigrat and heading toward Edaga Hamus, a town between Adigrat and Mekelle.

"I saw about 40 trucks carrying soldiers. The convoy was moving south," one resident of Adigrat, who requested anonymity for security reasons, told BBC Tigrinya.

A second resident reported seeing troop movements, initially at night: "We have been seeing trucks with Eritrean registration plates passing through the city.

"Now this morning we witnessed around 20 to 30 large trucks heading toward Edaga Hamus."

He added that acquaintances travelling along the route had seen additional vehicles carrying heavy weapons, including anti-aircraft guns, and noted some troops were also moving on foot.

A source in Mekelle told the BBC that relatives in Adigrat described even larger troop movements, and estimated they saw up to 60 trucks carrying soldiers who were later deployed in mountainous terrain near Edaga Hamus.

Images circulating on social media appear to show heavily loaded military trucks carrying uniformed personnel towards Adigrat, Edaga Hamus and possibly Wukro, another key town along the corridor between Adigrat and Mekelle. The BBC has not independently verified the images.

Sources in Wukro told the BBC that national army soldiers and allied fighters had entered the town on Wednesday after an exchange of heavy weapons about 15km south of the town.

The BBC has not yet been able to independently verify any of the reported troop movements.

The reported return of Eritrean forces has sparked anxiety among many of Tigray's residents, with some recalling the atrocities allegedly committed by soldiers from Eritrea during the recent civil war , when they fought against the TPLF.

One Adigrat resident said that seeing Eritrean soldiers again was emotionally distressing: "The memories are still fresh. I was emotional myself. People are saddened to see them back again."

A resident of Edaga Hamus also reported Eritrean troops passing through the town and said drone strikes had occurred nearby, with soldiers targeted.

In a recent interview with private station Fana Television, senior Ethiopian government official Abraham Belay accused Eritrea of direct participation in the conflict.

"The Eritrean army has participated with its full capacity and logistics," he said.

"Many Eritrean soldiers have been killed and captured. There is no doubt that the retaliation will be double. They will see what it means to enter the border of another country and fight alongside bandits."
